newsitem.title: UK: BFI down 22 points, chartering activity still slow.
newsitem.headline: BFI down 22 points, chartering activity still slow.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) fell 22 points to 1,292, with another day of slack chartering activity seen as the cause.

Despite this, the key U.S. Gulf/Japan heavy grain route looked to be holding steady. A 52,000-54,000 tonnes cargo was fixed by Seafreight at $22 for 15-28/5 shipment, unchanged from last reported for this size and shipment period.
However, as the Seafreight business was the only reported trade for this key route, brokers were uncertain whether this rate will hold.
Some felt though that problems with grain cargoes from the U.S. Gulf due to recent weather conditions was easing, and that an increase in shipments could be seen soon.
There was only one fresh coal fixture seen on Wednesday, which was Dieulemar's fixing of 140,000 tonnes coal Puerto Prodeco/Rotterdam 6-16 May at $6.
The component rates of the BFI pointed towards either unchanged or fractionally firmer levels.

On the timecharter side of the business, Brade Carriers took a 137,000 dwt vessel del China end April-early May for west Australia round trip at $10,000 daily. On Tuesday they took a 127,209 dwt vessel at the same price for the same trip.
The BIFFEX futures closed five firmer to 16 points below Tuesday's finish. Most active May traded last at 1,295, up five. May volume was 138 lots, while the total volume was 421 lots.
